content.title: The nature of evil and suffering
content.description: Follow a moderated exchange on evil, moral judgment and Christian hope amid suffering.

claim.text: Lennox distinguishes moral and natural evil and connects Christian hope with the resurrection. Shermer challenges religious explanations and advocates scientific and rational inquiry into suffering.

content.hinge: Are explanations of why harm occurs being used to answer the separate question of why it is morally wrong?
prompts: Distinguish moral evil from natural suffering.
Check how each speaker moves from explanation to moral judgment.
Separate a claim about hope from evidence for the belief behind it.
content.transcriptCoverage: Supplied text includes opening statements, moderated discussion, closing statements and audience questions. Original headings and wording are retained. Read the supplied text on this page; it has not been independently aligned word for word with the recording.

reviews.scope: Transcript source, event identity, editorial summary, coverage notes and YouTube metadata review
reviews.note: Checked linked transcript structures and publisher notices; compared participant/event descriptions with the recording listings. Verified YouTube metadata and runtimes on 2026-10-11; rejected a 9:12 Concept of God excerpt and selected the 1:31:47 debate. Summaries are editorial paraphrases. Full recordings were not watched or heard, and word-for-word alignment and whole-event completeness remain unverified. No external transcript body is republished. Existing doctrinal policy is unchanged.

reviews.scope: Owner-supplied transcript preservation, attribution and coverage
reviews.note: Saved the supplied text byte for byte with SHA-256 provenance. Explicit source labels and headings determine reader passages and sections. Hitchens text contains only his own statements. Krauss text also includes written post-debate reflections and footnotes, labelled separately from speech. Speaker attribution follows the supplied text and is not independently audio-verified. Full text and downloads are checked against the original source; previous documentary summary and doctrine unchanged.

reviews.scope: Text unchanged.
